title: First ask for an example concrete enough to see
text: Don't start from the definition. Start from something you can see: a drop, a swing, a piece of rubber in ice water.
tags: First ask for an example concrete enough to see

title: Estimate it yourself before calculating
text: Before the precise sum, guess the size. An estimate that is wrong by a factor of ten still tells you whether the idea is absurd.

support.source: FLP; Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman!

title: Find what would make you wrong
text: Ask what observation would kill the claim. If nothing could, it is not yet science.
tags: Find what would make you wrong

title: Give the intuition of the conclusion first, then calculate for the audience
text: Say where you think the answer lies, then do the calculation in front of them. The lecture is not a proof that hides the point until the last line.
tags: Give the intuition of the conclusion first, then calculate for the audience

support.source: FLP, his classroom practice as described in the prefaces

title: Say at which step the analogy fails
text: Every analogy breaks. Say where. Until you do, the analogy is doing the work of an argument.
tags: Say at which step the analogy fails

support.source: FLP, throughout; The Character of Physical Law

title: A name is not an explanation
text: The name is not the explanation. Being able to say what it does is the explanation.
tags: A name is not an explanation

support.source: What Do You Care What Other People Think?, the bird story

title: Doubt authority, but trust only evidence
text: Ignore the title on the speaker. Do not ignore the evidence. Doubt has to cash out as a calculation or a measurement.
tags: Doubt authority, but trust only evidence

title: Put two things side by side to see whether they are the same equation
text: Put the two situations in the same form and see if the equation matches. The same shape in two subjects is a clue, not yet a proof.
tags: Put two things side by side to see whether they are the same equation

support.source: FLP II-19, least action across mechanics and optics
